checks: The exact source hash matches cb7ea417552f0084 §7. The normalization reproduces its symmetric interval example and realizes it in every integer-base dimension by taking the displayed product. For n=0 the base factor is a singleton by the empty-product convention.

The base box contains only the integer site zero. The two affine cuts are genuine nested convex cuts and leave the measured interval [−1+ε,1−ε]. The ambient halfspaces cover and their only measured traces each have length 1−ε. At the old midpoint each therefore attains the old depth and each normalized mass stays exactly 1/2.

A containing ambient halfspace has, at the measured site, a halfline containing the mark or the whole line. Each tail based at the mark is realized by a closed ambient halfspace. The smaller tail length is 1−ε−ε² at the prescribed mark and 1−ε at the midpoint. The midpoint maximizes this smaller tail. The strict gap is ε² and the mark is interior since ε²<1−ε for 0<ε<1/2.

The one-dimensional retained-cap formula gives T=2(1−ε−ε²). Dividing by 2(1−ε) gives a difference quotient at zero of −ε/(1−ε), tending to zero. Independently checked ε=1/3 with raw depth 5/9 versus 2/3, retained mass 10/9, total mass 4/3 and ratio 5/6.

dependencies.mapping: Its dimension-one formula applies at the old midpoint and at the prescribed interior marks in the eroded intervals, with distances 1−ε+ε² and 1−ε−ε² from the two endpoints.

overlap.comparison: Supplies the static interval retained-mass formula, which gives the exact retained ratio after substitution. It has no critical-cover or deepest-path continuation assertion.

Its feasible barycenter interval implies the static retained formula by affine rescaling and maximization over the mass. Its separate counterexample concerns scalar barycenter compatibility, with no deformation or neutral-cover implication.

Its finite-cut theorem accommodates the elementary interval erosion and fixed halfspace losses. The reviewed claim concerns failure of a prescribed path to stay deepest despite exact normalized cover neutrality and zero retained slope.

readability: The old critical halfspaces are fixed as the mark moves. Depth is computed from halfspaces containing the new mark, which can have a different threshold.

summary: The one-fiber construction gives exact cover neutrality and zero normalized retained derivative, while the prescribed interior path loses a strictly positive amount of depth at every displayed positive parameter.
